blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A service keeps four connected ASCIIChannels in a pool, each with a read timeout of 2 seconds. A borrower sends a purchase and calls receive(); the host's answer leaves the host 2.6 seconds later. What becomes of that answer?

options.text: It is read by the next borrower of that channel, since a read timeout leaves the answer waiting in the connection
options.says: in 2.1.7 the channel closes its socket when the read timeout fires, so there is no open connection to wait in

options.text: It is lost before that borrower sees it, since the channel closed its connection when the read timeout fired
options.says: receive() threw SocketTimeoutException after 2 s and the channel closed the socket first; the answer goes into a connection that no longer exists

options.text: It is read by that same borrower after all, since receive() keeps waiting past the read timeout until a frame arrives
options.says: receive() never returns null and never waits past the read timeout: after 2 s of silence it throws

options.text: It is lost before that borrower sees it, since the host learns of the read timeout and never sends it
options.says: a read timeout is local to the client; the host knows nothing of it and sends the answer, which is lost on the client's side

origin.section: 3.3.1 Spot the Problem: A Pool of Channels

questions.stem: A ChannelAdaptor declares its channel as <channel class="org.jpos.iso.channel.ASCIIChannel" timeout="120000" packager="org.jpos.iso.packager.GenericPackager">, followed by host, port and packager-config. After how much silence does this channel give up on a read?

options.text: After 120000 ms, since the channel reads its settings from the attributes of <channel>
options.says: the channel reads only the <property> children of <channel>; the attribute is ignored

options.text: After 120000 ms, since Q2 copies each attribute of <channel> into the channel's configuration
options.says: Q2 builds the channel's configuration from the <property> children only

options.text: After 300000 ms, since the channel never reads that value and keeps its own default
options.says: the timeout attribute is ignored and BaseChannel's default read timeout of 300000 ms applies

options.text: After 300000 ms, since the channel reads that value but never goes below its own default
options.says: the channel does not read the attribute at all; a timeout property of 120000 would be used as given

questions.stem: A client link uses org.jpos.iso.GenericSSLSocketFactory. Its <channel> has the properties host, port, packager-config, socketFactory, keystore, storepassword and keypassword, with both passwords taken from the environment. A machine on the network path answers the connection with a self-signed certificate for CN=gateway.example.net. What happens?

options.text: The connection is set up and messages flow, since the factory accepts the certificate without examining it
options.says: serverauth defaults to false, and then the 2.1.7 factory accepts any certificate: the link is encrypted but not authenticated

options.text: The handshake fails, since the factory accepts only a certificate it has been told to trust
options.says: the factory checks trust only when serverauth is true; then the keystore holds the trusted certificates

options.text: The connection is set up and then closed, since the factory compares the CN with the host name after the handshake
options.says: the CN is compared only when serverauth is true; without it nothing is checked

options.text: The handshake fails, since Java accepts no self-signed certificate that has not been installed
options.says: the factory installs its own trust manager, which with serverauth false accepts any certificate; the JDK's trust store is not consulted

origin.section: 3.6 A TLS Channel Checks the Host Only When You Tell It To

questions.stem: Your client reaches a host through a ChannelAdaptor whose channel is a NACChannel with the host, port and packager-config properties. The host's team starts sending zero-length frames on links that have been idle for 30 seconds. What do you see after the first idle half-minute?

options.text: Nothing changes, since the channel skips an empty frame and reads on to the next message
options.says: only ASCIIChannel answers and skips a zero-length frame by itself; a binary channel needs expect-keep-alive

options.text: Nothing changes, since the adaptor answers the empty frames before the channel reads them
options.says: the adaptor's Receiver only calls the channel's receive(); it never sees a frame before the channel does

options.text: The link drops and waits for an operator, since the adaptor does not reconnect after a frame it cannot read
options.says: the adaptor reconnects after any receive failure, waiting reconnect-delay first

options.text: The link drops and reconnects, since the channel rejects an empty frame as a bad one
options.says: without expect-keep-alive, receive() throws ISOException 'receive length 0 seems strange' and the adaptor disconnects, then reconnects

origin.section: 3.2 One Read Is Not One Message

concepts: A pool of raw channels mixes answers between borrowers and loses the answers that come after a read timeout, because the 2.1.7 channel closes its socket when the timeout fires.
A timeout attribute on <channel> and a <ready> element on the adaptor are ignored: the read timeout is the timeout property, the ready key is always <name>.ready.
GenericSSLSocketFactory accepts any certificate unless serverauth is true, then trusts the keystore and compares servername with the CN; passwords come from the environment.
A zero-length frame is a keep-alive: ASCIIChannel skips it, a binary channel needs expect-keep-alive or the adaptor drops the link.
